analysis_pipeline: scripts/eval_v251_round.py - contrast, holm, exact_mcnemar, wilcoxon_signed_rank, paired_bootstrap, clopper_pearson imported, not re-derived

declared.rule: CLAUDE.md rule 8 - the seed count is fixed here and is not revisited after reading any endpoint; no extension of this panel may be reported as the same test

base.role: frozen pi0.5, Delta := 0, identical code path

rand.role: UNTRAINED random residual at the round's scale

M0.role: stale WM: transition trained on D0 only

M0_cont.role: stale WM + M1's extra optimiser budget, still D0 only

M1.role: updated WM: transition trained on D0 + D1

M1_shuf.role: updated WM with D1 action pairing broken

family_audit.resolution: the preregistration's multiplicity.family_secondary lists 15 tests over last_progress_step, phi_basin_mean, stage; d_min_final_atom is named under endpoint_hierarchy.secondary but carries no test in that family. It is therefore reported here with an interval and an UNCORRECTED p, labelled estimation-only, and it is NOT added to the Holm family - adding it would enlarge a registered family after the numbers were seen, and dropping the endpoint entirely would hide a registered quantity.

endpoint_tiers.rule: terminal success is reported for every arm with a Clopper-Pearson interval and is NOT a test at this n; the primary test is milestone-4 attainment; the secondary endpoints are supportive and are not confirmatory on their own
endpoint_tiers.statement: TESTS under this preregistration: milestone4 (primary family, 5 McNemar contrasts) and last_progress_step, phi_basin_mean, stage (secondary family, 15 Wilcoxon contrasts, Holm over that registered size). ESTIMATION-ONLY: success (the power block forbids reading it as a test at this n) and d_min_final_atom (a registered secondary endpoint with no test in the Holm family). The secondary family is supportive and is not confirmatory on its own.

per_arm_means.pairing: one shared (resamples, n) seed-index draw applied to every arm and endpoint
per_arm_means.percentiles: sorted means at int(0.025*B) and int(0.975*B), cluster_bootstrap's convention

success.label: terminal success
success.caveat: an ESTIMATION endpoint at this n, not a test: see the power block. Reported as a Clopper-Pearson interval per arm and a discordant-pair table, never as a verdict.

milestone4.label: milestone-4 attainment (pick_up cream_cheese_1)
milestone4.caveat: attaining the pick does not imply the place: milestone 5 was reached in 3/96. A milestone-4 gain that does not propagate is a gain in the approach, not in the task.

stage.label: contiguous stage reached
stage.caveat: 87/96 episodes sit on one value, so this endpoint is nearly constant and its Wilcoxon runs on few non-zero pairs.

last_progress_step.label: last-progress step
last_progress_step.caveat: confounded with pace: an arm that reaches the SAME milestones more slowly scores higher. Read it only together with `stage`.

phi_basin_mean.label: mean Phi' over the stall basin
phi_basin_mean.caveat: Phi' is a scripted privileged stand-in for human video annotation (lcwm/v250_progress.py). It is identical across arms so it cannot explain a difference, but any effect stated in it is scoped to 'under this supplied progress annotation'.
phi_basin_mean.missingness_note: null whenever the episode has final_atom_boundaries == 0, i.e. no boundary at which the final goal atom was active; the per-arm table below conditions on the seeds where ALL arms carry a value, which is itself outcome-dependent, so the per-arm available count is reported with it. The registered contrasts are NOT restricted to this subset: each uses its own pair's complete seeds, and every contrast reports n_paired.

d_min_final_atom.label: closest approach to the final goal object
d_min_final_atom.caveat: SIGN IS NEGATIVE: smaller is better. Counted only over boundaries where the final atom is the ACTIVE one - unrestricted, the same 24 base episodes read 9/24 within 5 cm instead of 0/24, because the minimum was the gripper beside a CAN during that can's placement. It is deliberately SECONDARY and must never be read as the outcome: on the calibration ladder it moved OPPOSITE to the outcome, with scale 1.60 giving the best approach of any arm (median 0.243 m, 20/24 seeds closer than base) while picking the object up half as often as scale 0.80 and never placing it. An arm can win this endpoint by driving the gripper at the object without ever closing on it.
d_min_final_atom.missingness_note: null whenever the episode has final_atom_boundaries == 0, i.e. no boundary at which the final goal atom was active; the per-arm table below conditions on the seeds where ALL arms carry a value, which is itself outcome-dependent, so the per-arm available count is reported with it. The registered contrasts are NOT restricted to this subset: each uses its own pair's complete seeds, and every contrast reports n_paired.

secondary_family_rejections.rule: Holm over the registered family of 15, two-sided; `favours` names the arm the ORIENTED difference points to, so a rejection against M1 is visible as such

wilcoxon_vs_mean_interval_disagreements.rule: the registered test is the Wilcoxon signed-rank; the CI is a bootstrap of the MEAN difference. Rows where the interval excludes zero and the Wilcoxon does not reach 0.05, or the reverse, are listed so neither is quoted as the other.

correctness_check.discrepancy_note: the discordant tables reproduce EXACTLY on all 5 published rows; 1 p-value(s) do not match the published digits: ['milestone4:M1-vs-base']. For M1-vs-base the pipeline's exact McNemar on b=34, c=7 is 2*P(X<=7 | Bin(41, 1/2)) = 2.5321e-05, which scipy.stats.binomtest reproduces to 1e-16, while the published figure 3.05e-05 is 2^-15 exactly. The recomputation is what eval_v251_round.exact_mcnemar returns from the surviving per-episode records; this report does not adjust it to the published digits, and the published figure is flagged rather than reconciled. The Holm-adjusted value changes with it: 5 x 2.5321e-05 = 1.266e-04 against the published 0.00015. Neither crosses any decision boundary, so no reported rejection changes.
